rv.q: In terms of the Great White Way, it is an anti-musical. Based on the 2007 film by John Carney , with a book by Enda Walsh and songs by Glen Hansard and Markéta Irglová, it is unusual not just in being given a stripped-down production by John Tiffany on a barroom set by Bob Crowley that is all scuffed mirrors, wooden panelling and gloomy corners.
Instead, with the ensemble on stage, performing a pre-show set, the lights slowly and softly fade, gently moving the audience into the world surrounding the show instead of the normal quick jolt.
